turns.user: Tin tức AI nổi bật hôm nay có gì?
turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là một số tin tức và thảo luận nổi bật về AI được ghi nhận hôm nay:

1. **Thị trường cổ phiếu AI phục hồi sau biến động**
   * Sau đợt bán tháo mạnh gần đây liên quan đến các yếu tố chính trị và thị trường, các cổ phiếu công nghệ và AI đang có xu hướng hồi phục. Nhiều tổ chức tài chính lớn như Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley và JPMorgan nhận định thị trường đã rơi vào vùng bán quá mức (oversold) và mở ra các cơ hội đầu tư mới, dù tâm lý thận trọng vẫn xuất hiện quanh vị thế và các vấn đề gần đây của Nvidia.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/10/ai-stocks-nvidia-broadcom) / [The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257)

2. **Rủi ro từ các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả mạo tạo bằng AI**
   * Công nghệ AI đang gây khó khăn lớn cho các cơ quan thực thi pháp luật trong việc phân biệt các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả mạo (swatting). Các công cụ AI ngày càng tinh vi trong việc tạo ra giọng nói và bối cảnh chân thực để báo cáo các vụ xả súng hoặc sự cố nguy hiểm không có thật, đặt ra thách thức an ninh mới.  
   * *Nguồn:* [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-5971477/ai-is-making-it-harder-to-detect-fake-emergency-calls)

3. **Cảnh báo về rủi ro từ lời khuyên y tế của AI dù nội dung có thể chính xác**
   * Các chuyên gia y tế cảnh báo rằng ngay cả khi mô hình AI cung cấp thông tin y khoa chính xác về mặt lý thuyết, cách diễn đạt và lựa chọn thông tin của AI vẫn có thể định hướng hành vi của người bệnh theo hướng rủi ro hoặc gây hại lâu dài. Giới chuyên môn kêu gọi cần có các chuẩn đánh giá hành vi (behavioral benchmarking) chặt chẽ hơn khi ứng dụng AI vào chăm sóc sức khỏe trực tiếp.  
   * *Nguồn:* [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years.

items.summary:
One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

items.title: AI stocks bounce back — with one notable exception
items.summary:
The AI trade has regained momentum despite — or maybe because of — Nvidia's struggles following the weekend revelations from CEO Jensen Huang.

The big picture: Monday's sudden burst of exuberance for AI was the latest wide swing for a market upended by last week's "blue tsunami" in the midterm elections and the threat they could pose to the data center boom. [...] "We believe stocks are now clearly in oversold territory," Goldman Sachs analysts wrote in a note Monday.
   "We believe the market's reaction to the midterms is overdone," wrote Morgan Stanley tech analysts in a note entitled "Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the U.S. Midterms," which it published Sunday night. [...] "We do not think AI is a continued sell here. In fact, tech drawdown is offering certain opportunities. The selloff was very sharp," JPMorgan equity strategists wrote Monday.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now les
items.summary:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

1. **Dự án "TristanTube" tạo trong 3 phút**  
   * **Nội dung:** Lấy cảm hứng từ danh sách các kênh YouTube hay do người dùng Tristan chia sẻ, Karpathy đã dùng Claude Code để tạo ra trang web "TristanTube" chỉ trong 3 phút ("one-shot"). Trang web tổng hợp 47.000 video chuyên sâu về công nghệ kèm chế độ "TV mode" tiện lợi để xem.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Xem tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2119114537442189652)

2. **Dự án cuối tuần: HackerTube**  
   * **Nội dung:** Vì không hài lòng với thuật toán gợi ý của YouTube, anh đã dùng Claude (Opus 5.5) lọc 43 triệu bình luận trong 20 năm qua trên Hacker News để chọn ra 6.454 video được cộng đồng đề xuất nhiều nhất. Toàn bộ quy trình lập trình, tối ưu, bảo mật và triển khai lên máy chủ VPS đều do AI tự động thực hiện chỉ trong khoảng 2 giờ; anh chỉ hỗ trợ tạo API key, thuê server và mua tên miền.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Xem tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2116957135661945283)

3. **Chia sẻ lại bài đăng về bảo mật Smart TV**  
   * **Nội dung:** Karpathy chia sẻ lại tweet của @Tristan0x giải thích lý do vì sao Smart TV hiện nay lại có giá thành rẻ như vậy, dẫn chứng từ việc một người dùng root TV Samsung và phát hiện micro thu âm luôn bật ở chế độ ngầm.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Xem tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2114384346815820050)

4. **Sự phân hóa sâu sắc về góc nhìn năng lực LLM**  
   * **Nội dung:** Anh phân tích về khoảng cách ngày càng mở rộng trong nhận thức của con người về năng lực AI (mô hình hình phễu):
     * ~75% dân số hầu như chưa từng tiếp xúc với LLM.
     * ~20% người dùng phổ thông chỉ coi AI như một chatbot tìm kiếm hoặc hỗ trợ viết lách thông thường.
     * ~0,2% (dân chuyên ngành lập trình/toán) đang chứng kiến AI hoàn thành các dự án lớn trong vài phút thay vì hàng tuần/tháng.
     * ~5.000 người trong các phòng thí nghiệm hàng đầu đang thấy các hệ thống đa agent tự giải quyết những bài toán khoa học và an ninh phức tạp ở tốc độ máy tính.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Xem tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2109361546505966046)

5. **Thử nghiệm đánh giá LLM: "Đất hay Nước?"**  
   * **Nội dung:** Một bài test đánh giá năng lực thú vị: chỉ cần đưa tọa độ kinh/vĩ độ và hỏi mô hình "Land or Water?" (Đất hay Nước) qua 16.200 lần rồi vẽ biểu đồ điểm ảnh. Kết quả cho thấy mô hình AI tái hiện được bản đồ thế giới nhờ vào khả năng nén thông tin từ toàn bộ dữ liệu internet.  
   * *Nguồn:* [Xem tweet](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2105909609487872075)

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now les
items.summary:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.
